name: Exercise the incident response plan on a stated cadence
description: Run a documented exercise of the response plan within each period, capture what did not work, and track the resulting improvements to closure.
responsible_role: Incident commander role, with the CISO or equivalent accountable

steps.action: State a test cadence and test type in the incident response policy.
Build a scenario against the entity's own systems and plausible threats rather than a generic template.
Run the exercise with the people the plan actually names, early in the period rather than near its end.
Record observations including what did not work, not only that the exercise took place.
Raise improvement actions with owners and target dates in the normal work tracker.
Confirm closure of the prior exercise's actions at the start of the next one.

implementation_considerations: A tabletop is cheap and sufficient for a first cycle; a functional test costs far more and is worth deferring until the plan survives a tabletop.
Schedule early in the period. A test run near period end leaves no room if it slips, which is how this control most often fails.
A real incident worked through the plan and documented frequently satisfies the same objective, though treatment varies by firm.
Scheduling the exercise is easy; getting the named roles into the room is the constraint. Book them first.
typical_duration: Half a day for a tabletop, plus a few days of preparation and write-up.
prerequisites: A documented response plan with assigned roles

verification_method.how: Confirm a test record dated within the examination period exists, containing scenario, participants covering the plan's roles, observations, and improvement actions with owners.

residual_risk_note: A tabletop exercises decision-making, not technical capability. It will not reveal that a recovery mechanism does not work.
period_limitation_note: A test cannot be performed retrospectively. Where no exercise occurred within an elapsed period, running one now evidences the next period, not the last.
notes: No test cadence is prescribed by SOC 2. The cadence the entity states is the benchmark for whether testing occurred as described.
